hints: Focus on what type of multiple bond each molecule has, since the number of pi bonds depends on single, double or triple bonds.
Remember propene has one C=C double bond, while both carbon dioxide and hydrogen cyanide have more multiple bonding than that.
Count one pi bond for every double bond and two pi bonds for every triple bond, then add them up for the whole molecule to find which have two in total.
walkthrough:
**Recall how pi bonds link to bond order**

A single bond is 1 sigma bond with no pi. A double bond is 1 sigma + 1 pi. A triple bond is 1 sigma + 2 pi.

Rule to use:
$$\text{double bond = 1 } \pi, \quad \text{triple bond = 2 } \pi$$

**Draw out the three molecules**

Propene is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2$ with one C=C double bond. Hydrogen cyanide is $\text{H-C}\equiv\text{N}$ with one C triple N bond. Carbon dioxide is $\text{O=C=O}$ with two C=O double bonds.

**Count the total pi bonds**

Propene: 1 double bond gives 1 pi bond. HCN: 1 triple bond gives 2 pi bonds. $\text{CO}_2$: 2 double bonds give 1 + 1 = 2 pi bonds.

So carbon dioxide and hydrogen cyanide each contain two pi bonds.

options.A: Correct. HCN has a $\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$ triple bond which contributes 2 pi bonds. $\text{CO}_2$ has two $\text{C=O}$ double bonds, each contributing 1 pi bond, for a total of 2 pi bonds.
options.B: Incorrect. While carbon dioxide does have two pi bonds, propene has only one pi bond from its single C=C double bond. This choice wrongly counts propene as having two.
options.C: Incorrect. Hydrogen cyanide does have two pi bonds, but propene has only one pi bond. Students choosing this often confuse an alkene double bond with a triple bond.
options.D: Incorrect. Hydrogen cyanide alone is incomplete because carbon dioxide also has two pi bonds in total. This trap comes from forgetting to add the pi bonds from both C=O bonds in $\text{O=C=O}$.
